en.title: Lee Chang-dong Drops First Trailer for Oscar Contender 'Possible Love'
en.summary: After an eight-year hiatus, the acclaimed director Lee Chang-dong is back with 'Possible Love,' South Korea's official Oscar entry. The first trailer offers a glimpse into this highly anticipated drama.
en.body:
The anticipation for **Lee Chang-dong’s** return has been palpable, and with the release of the first trailer for **Possible Love**, that excitement is set to reach a fever pitch. Eight years after his masterful and haunting **Burning**, Lee is back with what is undoubtedly one of the most anticipated films of the fall season. South Korea’s official Oscar entry, **Possible Love** clocks in at a substantial 164 minutes and promises a narrative as intricate and layered as the director’s previous works.

The film centers on two middle-aged couples from vastly different walks of life whose paths tragically, or perhaps inevitably, cross. We meet Mi-ok (**Jeon Do-yeon**) and Ho-seok (**Sul Kyung-gu**), a working-class couple bound by years of shared history since middle school. Their lives are currently overshadowed by the fallout from Ho-seok’s job loss following a violently suppressed labor union strike. Contrasting their struggles are the affluent Ye-ji (**Cho Yeo-jeong**) and Sang-woo (**Zo In-sung**). Ye-ji, a documentary filmmaker, decides to make a film about job layoffs, choosing Mi-ok and Ho-seok as her primary subjects. This decision ignites a brilliantly unfolding narrative, forcing both marriages to confront their hidden desires, simmering resentments, and shifting allegiances.

The trailer hints at a complex exploration of nonfiction filmmaking ethics, as Ye-ji’s camera captures the raw realities of Mi-ok and Ho-seok’s lives. The New York Film Festival synopsis eloquently describes the film as a story that "pierces the heart of contemporary South Korea, laying bare the scars of personal trauma and socioeconomic grievance." It promises a story rich with sexual tensions and profound questions about truth, representation, and the very nature of documenting human experience. Anchored by what are sure to be four towering performances, **Possible Love** is shaping up to be another essential piece of cinema from a director who consistently delivers profound and unforgettable works.

## A Master's Return Ignites Global Buzz

Fans of **Lee Chang-dong** have been eagerly awaiting his next directorial effort since the critically acclaimed **Burning** captivated audiences and critics alike in 2018. Known for his unflinching gaze into the complexities of the human psyche and the societal undercurrents of South Korea, Lee’s return is a significant event in the film world. The release of the trailer, coupled with its selection as South Korea’s Oscar entry, amplifies the stakes and the global interest. This isn't just another film; it's a statement from one of contemporary cinema's most vital voices, offering a potential deep dive into themes that resonate universally: love, loss, economic disparity, and the blurred lines between reality and its depiction.

## What to Expect from Possible Love

With its theatrical release set for October 23 and a subsequent drop on Netflix on November 6, **Possible Love** is poised to make a significant impact. Following premieres at Venice, TIFF, and NYFF, the film’s trajectory suggests a powerful awards season run. Audiences can anticipate a character-driven drama that eschews easy answers, instead opting for nuanced portrayals and a lingering emotional resonance that is characteristic of **Lee Chang-dong’s** masterful storytelling. Prepare for a film that will undoubtedly spark conversations and linger in the mind long after the credits roll.

content_raw: Eight years after his masterful Burning , Lee Chang-dong’s Possible Love is certainly our most-anticipated film to premiere this fall . Clocking in at 164 minutes, it follows two married couples—a laid-off worker and his wife, and a documentary filmmaker and her husband—whose paths cross when the filmmaker sets out to document them, bringing both marriages face to face with their different lives and hidden desires. Ahead of Venice, TIFF, and NYFF premieres, Netflix has now released the first trailer for South Korea’s Oscar entry, which will drop on their platform on November 6 following an October 23 theatrical release. Here’s the New York Film Festival synopsis: “In such searing dramas as Secret Sunshine (NYFF45) and Burning (NYFF56), the great filmmaker Lee Chang-dong pierces the heart of contemporary South Korea, laying bare the scars of personal trauma and socioeconomic grievance. His extraordinary latest concerns two middle-aged couples from different walks of life who become unlikely acquaintances. Working-class Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) and Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu), who have been together since middle school and are the parents of a taciturn 10-year-old, are still reckoning with the fallout from Ho-seok’s firing from his factory job after a violently suppressed labor union strike. The well-off Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong) and Sang-woo (Zo In-sung) are a documentary filmmaker and her businessman husband; Ye-ji has decided to make a movie about job layoffs and wants to make Mi-ok and Ho-seok her main camera subjects. The result is a brilliantly unfolding narrative of simmering resentments, shifting allegiances, sexual tensions, and queries around nonfiction filmmaking ethics that keeps revealing new layers and meanings, anchored by four towering performances that hit a varying array of fragile emotional registers. Possible Love speaks profoundly to our shared current moment of emotional and economic precarity. A Netflix release.” See the trailer below.
